claims.text: Explicitly incorporating hierarchical microstructural features will improve prediction accuracy for HfNbTiVAl10 relative to homogenized continuum models.
Explicitly incorporating hierarchical microstructural features will make predictions for HfNbTiVAl10 faster than established homogenized continuum models.
As-fabricated HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure containing intragranular nanoprecipitates and a primary matrix phase.
The hierarchical arrangement of nanoprecipitates and matrix phases mediates dislocation motion.
The hierarchical arrangement of nanoprecipitates and matrix phases governs local stress concentrations.
Nanoprecipitates act as barriers to dislocation dynamics.
Explicitly modeling nanoprecipitate barrier effects and heterogeneous-interface stress fields will better capture strain localization.
Explicitly modeling nanoprecipitate barrier effects and heterogeneous-interface stress fields will better capture yielding.
Explicitly modeling nanoprecipitate barrier effects and heterogeneous-interface stress fields will better capture crack nucleation.
Greater microscale fidelity reduces reliance on empirical homogenization.
Greater microscale fidelity reduces computational overhead.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness within approximately ±5% of experimental measurements.
The proposed model will reduce simulation time by approximately 30–50% relative to established methods.
Established continuum or homogenized methods typically have prediction uncertainties of approximately ±10%.
Established continuum or homogenized methods require greater computational resources than the proposed model.
Dynamic phase transformations may cause the proposed model to fail when they dominate material response.
Strong temperature or deformation-rate dependencies may cause the proposed model to fail.
Inaccurate characterization of hierarchical features may cause the proposed model to fail.
